allOf.description: The simulated-spill audit lie, killed in the schema: a page that was absorbed (simulated:true) never went on the wire, so it cannot carry a wire failure outcome. simulated:true REQUIRES outcome 'accepted' and forbids error_class. A failure for an unattempted page is unrepresentable.
B3: degraded-channel receipts carry the replay-dedup key.
B3: spill_id is meaningless off the degraded channel.

description: What L5 did with one delivery attempt, reported to L6. ATOMICITY (behavioral, normative) — OUTBOX-BACKED CHANNELS (outbox, secondary): the receipt MUST be written in the SAME database transaction as the outbox scheduler update it describes (claim/confirm/retry/dead-letter). A receipt without its scheduler row, or a scheduler row without its receipt, is a contract violation — the event log and the work queue can never disagree (I2, event-log-audit.md §1.1). DEGRADED CHANNEL (direct-degraded): there is NO scheduler row by design — the atomicity rule does not apply here. The honest guarantee is AT-LEAST-ONCE REPLAY: every spill file is replayed into the event log until its file is archived; a crash between the log append and the file archive MAY emit a duplicate receipt for one send (mechanically demonstrated by crash injection). L6 MUST deduplicate degraded-channel receipts on (channel, spill_id): same channel + same spill_id is the same send replayed — keep first, drop the rest. SIMULATED HONESTY (normative): simulated:true MUST propagate end-to-end and MUST NEVER be recorded as a failure. The simulated-spill audit lie (forwarder-byok.md §2.5) dies at this contract: any path that emits a failure event for a page that was never attempted on the wire falsifies the contract.

attempt_no.description: 1-based attempt number, taken from the outbox row's attempt_count at claim time (forwarder.py:444). Counts both primary and secondary channels; shared with the retry schedule index (attempt_no - 1). On the direct-degraded channel attempt_no is always 1: the degraded path makes exactly one direct attempt (no retry ladder); duplicate suppression across crash-replays is spill_id's job, not attempt_no's.

channel.description: Which delivery path produced this receipt. 'outbox' = durable outbox → PagerDuty; 'direct-degraded' = send_direct fail-open backstop (outbox unavailable); 'secondary' = secondary channel after primary exhaustion.

spill_id.description: REQUIRED when channel is direct-degraded; FORBIDDEN on outbox/secondary. sha256 (lowercase hex) of the spill file's exact bytes as read at replay. Stable across crash-replays of the same spill (same file → same bytes → same id); unique across distinct spill writes. This is the replay-dedup key L6 uses: attempt_no is always 1 on the degraded path (single direct attempt, no retry ladder), so repeated degraded sends are indistinguishable from duplicate replays without it.

contract.description: Self-identifying contract name on the wire.

contract_version.description: Additive-only inside a version; a true break takes a new version (C7 compat rule, OPERATING-RULES §1.1).

decision_id.description: The event-log sequence number of the decision_made event being acted on, rendered as a decimal string (e.g. "412"). MINT — defined normatively here, the single contract that defines it: (a) outbox/secondary channels: L5 reads the outbox row's decision_seq column (INTEGER NOT NULL, eventlog.py:282) and renders it decimal; (b) direct-degraded channel: there is no outbox row — L5 MUST capture the decision's event-log sequence into the spill record (spill field decision_seq) at send time, and the replay MUST copy it verbatim into the receipt. The value "-1" means NO joinable decision: control-plane pages (eventlog.py _enqueue_control_plane_page) and degraded sends whose decision never durably sequenced (e.g. the commit-watchdog path). L6 joins receipt → decision_made on this key; "-1" receipts stand alone.

error_class.description: REQUIRED when outcome is retryable/terminal (e.g. 'timeout', 'rate_limited', 'max_age_exceeded', 'dedup_key_invalid', 'secondary_failed', 'degraded_send_failed'). FORBIDDEN when outcome is accepted — an accepted receipt carries no error. This rule is what makes 'failure' machine-detectable and what the simulated-spill lie tried to fake.

outcome.description: Wire outcome, using pd_sender's own taxonomy (pd_sender.py:91 — accepted | retryable | terminal; Chesterton's fence: reuse the taxonomy the code already speaks). 'accepted' covers real wire acceptance AND simulated absorption (distinguished by the simulated flag). Retryable/terminal MUST carry error_class.

simulated.description: true iff the page was ABSORBED by simulated mode (nothing sent to the wire; forwarder.py:766 'pd_outcome: simulated'). The flag MUST propagate through spill replay into the event body. simulated:true + outcome accepted is a CONFIRMATION of absorption, never a failure. Consumers MUST NOT map simulated:true to any failure metric, SLO burn, or forward_failed event.

wire_sha256.description: sha256 of the EXACT bytes presented to the transport (pd_sender.py:338 hashes `wire`, the exact POST body). For SIMULATED absorption: sha256 of the CANONICAL KEYLESS serialization — the wire event as constructed on the simulated path (which never resolves a routing key; the key value is deliberately never materialized) serialized as JSON with keys sorted, separators (',',':'), UTF-8 encoded. The producer MUST construct these exact bytes on the simulated path even though nothing is transmitted; this is what keeps simulated receipts comparable and what the §3.4 byte-equality test checks against independently-constructed keyless bytes. Never a re-serialization of pretty-printed JSON, never a hash of an arbitrary placeholder: an unconstructible wire_sha256 is a contract violation.
